desc:
A board is a string made of the characters L, R and X, where X is an empty cell. You may repeat the following moves any number of times:

  • replace a substring XL by LX (an L slides one cell to the left into an empty cell),
  • replace a substring RX by XR (an R slides one cell to the right into an empty cell).

Given two boards start and end of the same length, return true if end can be reached from start by such moves, otherwise false.

For example, "XLXRX" can become "LXXXR" (true), but "RXL" cannot become "LXR" (false): tokens never pass each other.
constraints: start and end contain only the characters L, R and X
hints: Searching all reachable boards explodes quickly. Look for invariants of the moves instead.
Tokens never jump over each other, so the sequence of L/R letters (ignoring X) cannot change.

Match the k-th non-X character of start with the k-th non-X character of end using two pointers. An L can only move left, so its index in end must not be larger than in start; an R can only move right, so its index in end must not be smaller.
editorial: Because L only swaps with an X on its left and R only with an X on its right, no two tokens can ever cross. Hence the sequence of tokens with the Xs removed is invariant, and the k-th token of start must become the k-th token of end.

Additionally, the k-th token can only travel in its own direction: if it is an L its position in end must be at most its position in start; if it is an R it must be at least. These conditions are also sufficient, since each token can walk to its destination through the gaps that the order-preserving matching leaves free. Two pointers that skip X implement the check in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
